question: What is the primary defining characteristic of essential medicines according to global health standards?

options.A: They are exclusively manufactured within national borders
options.B: They satisfy the priority healthcare needs of the population
options.C: They must be provided free of charge at all public facilities
options.D: They consist only of herbal and traditional formulations

explanation: Essential medicines are specifically chosen because they target the most prevalent health conditions in a community and offer proven therapeutic value. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why did the World Health Organization introduce the concept of essential medicines in the late 1970s?

options.A: To completely replace traditional healers with western medical practitioners
options.B: To establish a global monopoly on the production of antibiotics
options.C: To optimize limited resources by focusing on high-priority pharmaceutical needs
options.D: To eliminate the need for clinical trials in developing countries

explanation: The framework was designed to help resource-constrained health systems manage budgets efficiently by stocking only medicines with proven public health impact. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which factor is NOT considered when selecting an essential medicine?
explanation: Essential drug selection is strictly based on clinical necessity, public health impact, and affordability rather than commercial branding or aesthetics. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: When are fixed-dose combination products preferred on an essential medicines list?

options.A: When the individual components have conflicting pharmacological properties
options.B: When patients prefer taking fewer tablets regardless of clinical outcome
options.C: When the manufacturer offers a discount for bulk purchase
options.D: When they provide superior compliance, safety, or efficacy compared to single drugs

explanation: Combinations are only prioritized if grouping medicines together offers a tangible medical advantage, such as improved adherence in chronic disease regimens. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a major financial advantage of utilizing an essential drug list in public procurement?

options.A: Hospitals can sell surplus medications for profit to private pharmacies
options.B: Bulk purchasing of generic drugs drives down unit prices
options.C: Governments receive tax exemptions from international pharmaceutical companies
options.D: Patients are guaranteed completely free healthcare services indefinitely

explanation: Standardizing around essential generic equivalents allows health systems to leverage economies of scale during procurement. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: A clinic nurse notices that prescribers frequently make medication errors due to confusion among dozens of similar brand-name drugs. Which intervention directly addresses this issue?

options.A: Encouraging patients to purchase medications independently from patent medicine vendors
options.B: Ordering higher quantities of expensive imported brand-name medications
options.C: Restricting the facility inventory to a standardized essential medicines list
options.D: Increasing the variety of pharmaceutical manufacturers supplying the clinic

explanation: Limiting available stock to a concise list of well-known essential drugs reduces prescriber confusion and builds deep familiarity with dosages and side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a frequent operational challenge faced by health facilities regarding essential drugs?

options.A: Immediate obsolescence of all listed medications within a six-month window
options.B: Excessive manufacturing surpluses that overwhelm hospital warehouses
options.C: Prolonged stockouts caused by supply chain bottlenecks and transport failures
options.D: Complete lack of generic drug manufacturers worldwide

explanation: Poor logistics and distribution infrastructure frequently hinder the physical availability of essential medicines at peripheral health centers. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why might a patient express skepticism toward an essential generic medicine in favor of a branded alternative?

options.A: Essential drugs are chemically inert and contain no active pharmaceutical ingredients
options.B: A misconception that lower cost equates to inferior therapeutic quality
options.C: Branded medications always have fewer side effects than generic counterparts
options.D: Mandatory government regulations requiring patients to trial branded drugs first

explanation: Public perception sometimes wrongly links affordability to poor quality, leading patients to distrust inexpensive generic medications. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: What financial mechanism is commonly used in Nigerian public health institutions to maintain a continuous supply of essential drugs?
explanation: The DRF model uses revenue generated from medication sales to perpetually repurchase essential stock, maintaining inventory without relying on constant government bailouts. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which regulatory agency in Nigeria plays a critical role in safeguarding the quality of essential medicines by combating counterfeit products?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN)
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

explanation: NAFDAC is the statutory body responsible for regulating and controlling the manufacture, importation, exportation, distribution, and sale of drugs in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)
